title: Banteay Srei
visualBrief: Banteay Srei medium-fi surviving exterior: three stepped pink-sandstone sanctuary towers and lotus finials, recessed/false doors with curved pediments, eastern mandapa, two corbel-roofed libraries, inner gateways, lower outer/approach gateway remains and concentric stone/laterite enclosure traces. Native map moat and paths remain independent. Fine narrative sculpture, individual carved figures and exact damage inventories are not reproduced.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Q790099/way227968458 identifies the temple complex. Standard PMTiles building35184600057289 controls the central27×24m platform envelope; native moat polygon406679270 and the named east–west causeway constrain the overall plan. The three-tower photograph is explicitly from the west, showing false west doors; the principal entrance faces east along the mapped causeway. Other component locations are proportional visualization estimates within this frame, not separate surveyed building polygons.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Photographic proportions estimate central tower11.2m and flanking towers9.8m above their bases; libraries and gateways4–6m, lower outer ruins1–3m.
